decision_rule: Expose authoritative source products and their limitations before deriving any site metric. A product being listed here does not mean it has been downloaded, calibrated, spatially crosswalked, or validated for a current landing ellipse. Preserve the historical leads as source-reported clues, not repository-computed measurements; their time windows, heights, and interpretation boundaries must travel with any reuse.
metric_policy: No derived site metrics or site rankings are asserted by this catalogue. Keep candidate values unknown until source bytes, labels, spatial masks, units, resolution, acquisition/model epoch, uncertainty, and transformation provenance are verified.

sources.title: High-Resolution LOLA Topography for Lunar South Pole Sites
sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Planetary Geology, Geophysics and Geochemistry Laboratory
sources.spatial_resolution: 5 m/pixel GeoTIFF for raster products; XYZI point clouds and ROI shapefiles are exceptions
sources.coordinate_reference: South-polar stereographic X/Y in metres; MOON_ME reference frame, DE421 ephemeris. Verify each product label and README before reprojection or measurement.
sources.temporal_scope: Topographic model derived from historical LRO-LOLA tracks; not a mission-date illumination series.
uncertainty_and_limitations: The PGDA description reports around 90% interpolated 5 m pixels in these polar LDEMs.
Across listed regions, reported median RMS height uncertainty is approximately 0.30–0.50 m and median RMS slope uncertainty approximately 1.5–2.5 degrees.
Interpolation uncertainty varies with track gaps and terrain slope; a nominal 5 m pixel size is not 5 m independent measurement spacing.
The published region names and ROI boundaries are legacy research products; do not assume they are identical to currently named Artemis landing regions without an explicit spatial crosswalk.

candidate_crosswalk.product_site: Site01: Connecting ridge; legacy ROI boundaries
Site11: de Gerlache rim; SL2: de Gerlache rim

required_acceptance_checks: Capture exact file URL, filename, HTTP/content metadata where available, SHA-256, product-label URL and retrieval timestamp.
Read and verify raster CRS, transform, dimensions, pixel registration, nodata and scale/offset values from labels/metadata.
Use the supplied ROI files or an independently sourced, versioned region polygon; never derive the polygon from the place name.
Check raster dimensions, CRS compatibility, nodata, uncertainty-layer alignment and pixel registration before any zonal statistic.
Label name matches as provisional until ROI overlap and region identity are confirmed.

sources.title: Lunar Polar Illumination
sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / LOLA Planetary Data System
product_families: Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, GeoTIFF and other distribution formats
sources.spatial_resolution: South-polar products include 240 m/pixel for 65°S–90°S, 120 m/pixel for 75°S–90°S and 60 m/pixel for 85°S–90°S; confirm the selected raster's label.
sources.coordinate_reference: Polar stereographic projection, reference radius 1737.4 km and true scale at the pole; verify exact raster labels before alignment with LOLA site DEMs.
sources.temporal_scope: Several products are averages over an approximately 18.6-year lunar nutation cycle, not a mission-specific timeline.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Long-period averages can screen regions but cannot replace date-specific lighting analysis at the planned lander, habitat or rover height.
Earth visibility is defined by whether any part of Earth's disc is unobscured and can be optimistic for a specific radio link budget or ground-station geometry.
NASA notes that Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF overviews average the full-resolution values; quantitative analysis must sample full-resolution data rather than zoomed-out overviews.

candidate_crosswalk.note: The product supplies broad polar-band rasters; a candidate-specific value still requires an exact ROI, product-label/CRS verification, and full-resolution sampling.

sources.recommended_use: Use for an initial coarse layer and permanent-shadow context, explicitly labelled as long-period mean. For operations, derive or obtain epoch-specific illumination and communication visibility.
required_acceptance_checks: Verify band identity, unit/scale/offset, nodata, CRS, pixel registration and full-resolution block reads from the product labels.
Reject use of a time-averaged illumination value as a mission-window guarantee.
For radio planning, pair Earth-visibility geometry with antenna/link-budget analysis and relay geometry.

sample_direct_assets.title: 85S–90S average Earth visibility raster
sample_direct_assets.note: Earth-disc visibility is not itself a radio link budget; confirm label semantics and units before use.

asset_access_notes: On 2026-10-12, the sampled PGDA COG URL for AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608_COG.TIF returned an HTML 404 response in the browser check. This records one sampled URL failure only; it does not establish that every COG or TIFF product is unavailable.

The NASA PGDA product page links the LOLA PDS data node and describes IMG/GeoJPEG2000 distributions. The MIT PDS JP2 directory lists the above raster and label filenames. The browser tool could not render the binary or label endpoints, so no payload, PDS label field, checksum or numerical raster value has yet been verified here.

Do not infer meaning solely from AVGVISIB filename tokens. Read and validate the associated PDS label (including PRODUCT_ID, units/scaling, dimensions and projection) before mapping it to an illumination metric.

sources.title: South Pole LOLA DEM Mosaic
sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Planetary Geology, Geophysics and Geochemistry Laboratory
sources.spatial_resolution: 5 m/pixel GeoTIFF; source page reports approximately 3.3 GB elevation, 820 MB hillshade, 4.9 GB slope and 140 MB count products.
sources.coordinate_reference: South-polar stereographic X/Y in metres; MOON_ME, DE421; pixel-registered convention with X/Y at pixel centres.
sources.temporal_scope: Static terrain mosaic constructed from 97 overlapping 20 km fields; not a time series.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Coverage is 87°S–90°S, so it does not cover every candidate region in the register.
The page reports a typical RMS residual of 30–55 cm against the individual fields after alignment and blending.
The DEM interpolates empty pixels. Its nominal grid spacing must not be interpreted as uniform independent terrain measurement coverage.
The files are large; use windowed/COG access where supported rather than requiring every consumer to download all rasters.

candidate_crosswalk.note: This mosaic is not a substitute for per-region coverage checks and must not be assumed to cover all candidate regions.

sources.recommended_use: High-resolution topographic context for eligible southern areas; do not substitute it for absent candidate ROI boundaries or infer full coverage for Mons Mouton or other sites.
required_acceptance_checks: Verify geographic bounds and actual ROI intersection before computing a candidate statistic.
Read raster metadata and labels, confirm units, nodata and registration, and pin the asset SHA-256.
Record the exact window/mask and all excluded or interpolated cells in the output receipt.

sources.title: Illumination at the Moon's South Pole to 80°S, 2025–2028
product_families: rendered frame sets at two-hour intervals
sources.spatial_resolution: Rendered visualization products; frame resolution is not equivalent to source terrain resolution.
sources.coordinate_reference: Visualization covers the lunar south polar region; do not treat pixels in rendered movies or images as a georeferenced analysis raster unless a separate georeferencing method is documented.
sources.temporal_scope: Visualizations are labelled 2025, 2026, 2027 and 2028 with two-hour temporal steps across each year.
uncertainty_and_limitations: These are useful for communicating and visually checking illumination sequences, not a replacement for the numerical terrain/illumination model or data labels.
Do not digitize video pixels to create site illumination percentages or claim exact local conditions from a regional animation.

candidate_crosswalk.note: The rendered movie/frame series is not a georeferenced analysis raster and cannot supply numerical illumination metrics.

sources.recommended_use: Link as a qualitative orientation resource alongside machine-readable LOLA/illumination data.
required_acceptance_checks: Keep every value extracted from imagery explicitly classified as visual interpretation, not an authoritative measurement.
No pixel-derived numerical site metrics are accepted into the candidate register.

ingestion_sequence: Resolve exact candidate-region polygons and their published versions before drawing or clipping site rasters.
Inventory and hash source assets and parse labels/metadata before analysis.
Ingest per-site LDEM, slope, elevation uncertainty, slope uncertainty, LOLA count and clone ensemble as aligned layers where available.
Add long-period illumination/PSR/Earth-visibility products only as coarse screening layers, preserving their averaging window and pixel scale.
Compute epoch-specific lighting, cold-soak and traverse/relay constraints only after a documented mission epoch, height, path, coordinate frame and geometry model are supplied.
Emit each derived result with input checksums, transform and mask versions, units, statistic, uncertainty treatment, excluded area, software version and a replayable receipt.

historical_leads.title: Test Connecting Ridge / Site 01 as a historical comparator
historical_leads.related_region: Site01: Connecting ridge; legacy LOLA product ROI boundaries
historical_leads.finding: The PGDA product description reports that, from 2024-01-01 through 2026-01-01, Site 1 had the largest area with average illumination greater than 70% at 1 m above the surface among the compared sites; ROIs 4–6 at this site generally had favorable illumination even when uncertainty was considered. The page also reports longer continuous illumination periods at 5 m above the surface for Site 1.
historical_leads.next_action: Keep as a named historical comparator and retrieve the Site01 ROI shapefile and uncertainty-clone products before any same-method reanalysis.
interpretation_limits: This is a historical illumination comparison, not an evaluation for a future crewed mission window.
The result covers illumination only; it does not establish touchdown roughness, safe approach corridors, surface operations, communications link margin, thermal survival or resource access.
Site01 / ROI4–6 are legacy research identifiers. Spatial boundaries and compatibility with any modern agency candidate region must be explicitly validated.
The original page result has not been independently recomputed in this repository. Preserve it as a source-reported finding, not a new measurement.

historical_leads.title: Treat DEM pixel size separately from terrain certainty
historical_leads.related_region: All regions using the high-resolution LOLA site products
historical_leads.finding: NASA PGDA states that around 90% of pixels in the described 5 m/pixel polar LDEMs are interpolated and reports median RMS height uncertainty around 0.30–0.50 m and median RMS slope uncertainty around 1.5–2.5 degrees across the cited regions.
historical_leads.time_window: Static topographic product; verify individual asset labels and retrieval version
historical_leads.next_action: Carry uncertainty layers, LOLA return-count maps and clone ensembles into every zonal estimate; never report nominal 5 m pixel pitch as 5 m independent measurement spacing.
interpretation_limits: Summary uncertainty values are regional descriptions from the product page; they are not per-pixel errors or candidate-specific safety limits.
Interpolation error varies spatially with data gaps and terrain slope.

historical_leads.title: Keep long-period illumination separate from mission-window illumination
historical_leads.finding: NASA's polar illumination product page describes several illumination, permanent-shadow and Earth-visibility products as averages over an approximately 18.6-year lunar nutation cycle, and warns that further analysis is needed for shorter periods, greater resolution and height above the surface.
historical_leads.time_window: Approximately 18.6-year cycle averages for applicable products
historical_leads.next_action: Use the products only for coarse screening; obtain or compute a mission-epoch timeline at the relevant lander, habitat and rover heights before comparing energy storage or direct-to-Earth availability.
interpretation_limits: An average does not describe illumination continuity, longest darkness interval or the power-storage requirement for a given mission period.
Earth-disc visibility is not by itself a communications link budget or relay geometry.
